global_domain.empty_support: The all-zero matrix on the still nonempty index sets X and Y.
local_conventions: Allow factor dimension k=0 and define the empty disjunction as 0.
Allow the empty rectangle and biclique cover families.
For zero-support functions adopt a depth-zero constant-reject protocol with complexity 0.

concepts.definition: A records a finite binary relation through its 1-support.
The least k>=0 admitting A[x,y]=OR over l=1..k of (U[x,l] AND V[l,y]), with Boolean factors U,V.
The smallest number of all-one rectangles S times T whose union equals the 1-support. Arbitrary overlap on 1-cells is allowed.
concepts.source_symbol_mapping: Atlas rc_1 is S2 kappa(A). The Atlas subscript names the covered cell value; it does not impose the multiplicity-one condition denoted kappa_1(A) in S2.

concepts.definition: The minimum number of edge-bearing complete bipartite subgraphs covering all edges of a finite simple graph with fixed labeled disjoint sides X and Y. Use its biadjacency matrix A_G, not the full symmetric adjacency matrix.
S2 n(f): minimum maximum leaf depth of a nondeterministic protocol accepting exactly the 1-inputs, under the paper's local row/column leaf-test convention.
concepts.source_symbol_mapping: The Atlas superscript 1 identifies the accepted side. It is unrelated to S2 subscript n_1(f), which restricts each input to at most one witness.
concepts.complement_definition: Define N^0_S2(f):=N^1_S2(1-f), corresponding to S2 n(complement f). This superscript notation is an Atlas definition.

relationships.forward_witness: Each factor index l gives S_l={x:U[x,l]=1} and T_l={y:V[l,y]=1}. Their rectangular supports contain no zero of A and their union is its support; empty factors may be omitted.
relationships.reverse_witness: For each selected rectangle choose the indicator column of S_l and indicator row of T_l. Their Boolean OR-AND product reconstructs A.
relationships.zero_case_local_proof: When A is all-zero, k=0 reconstructs A by empty OR, and the empty rectangle family covers its empty support. Both objectives are nonnegative, so both minima are 0.

conditions: fixed labeled bipartition X disjoint-union Y
relationships.witness_translation: S times T corresponds to the biclique with vertex sides S subset X and T subset Y. Rectangle cells correspond one-to-one to graph edges. The translation preserves cover cardinality in both directions.
relationships.zero_case_local_proof: An edgeless graph on nonempty X,Y has the empty edge cover and empty rectangle cover. Nonnegative cardinalities force both minima to be 0.

relationships.statement_nonzero: N^1_S2(f)=ceil(log_2(rc_1(M_f))) when f has at least one 1-input
relationships.cover_to_protocol: For a cover with t>=1 rectangles, the first party nondeterministically names a rectangle compatible with its row, using ceil(log_2 t) bits, and the second party checks membership of its column. Rejection is allowed when no compatible choice succeeds. This is the cited protocol convention, not a convention-independent certificate-cost statement.
relationships.protocol_to_cover: Accepting leaves supply all-one rectangles covering the 1-inputs. A binary protocol of maximum depth h has at most 2^h leaves, yielding rc_1(M_f)<=2^h.
relationships.zero_case_local_proof: For all-zero f, an empty rectangle family gives rc_1=0. A depth-zero constant-reject protocol is sound and complete because there are no 1-inputs. Nonnegative depth gives N^1_S2=0.
relationships.local_totalization: Combining the cited nonzero statement with the separately proved local zero convention gives N^1_S2(f)=ceil(log_2(max(1,rc_1(M_f)))).
distinct_parameters: S2 kappa_1 counts a multiplicity-one cover, equivalent to a rectangle partition
S2 n_1 imposes at most one witness per input

relationships.definitions: lr_B minimizes, over all-one rectangle covers, the maximum number of chosen rectangles containing any row or column. lbc minimizes, over biclique edge covers, the maximum number of chosen bicliques containing any vertex.
relationships.witness_translation: The objectwise translation in R2 preserves participation of every row/column as participation of the corresponding graph vertex. Thus every cover has the same maximum incidence before and after translation, in both directions.
relationships.zero_case_local_proof: The empty cover assigns load 0 to every row, column and vertex. X and Y are nonempty, so the maximum is defined and equals 0; nonnegative loads make it minimal.
